retrieval_ref._about: Part 05 (retrieval, memory, context construction) reference-system values. Agree with RA-22 to RA-26.

chunks_per_document_mean.note: Workspace mixes short memos and long reports; 24 chunks of about 550 tokens is a document of about 13,000 tokens on average.

chunk_tokens_mean.note: Mean chunk length inside the 300-800 token range of RA-22.

acl_readable_fraction.note: Share of the tenant's 4,200 workspace documents whose ACL principals include the reference user or one of the user's groups.

hnsw_m.note: RA-24; equals the pgvector and Elasticsearch default.

hnsw_ef_construction.note: RA-24; higher than the pgvector (64) and Elasticsearch (100) defaults for build-time recall near 1.

hnsw_ef_search.note: Must be at least the per-retriever top-k (100) so the vector retriever can return 100 candidates.

per_retriever_top_k.note: BM25 and the vector index each return 100 candidates to fusion (RA-25).

rerank_keep.note: RA-25: keep the top 20 after reranking, then trim to the token budget.

query_embed_tokens.note: Task instruction plus the rewritten retrieval query on the query side of M-embed.

rerank_template_tokens.note: Instruction, query and chat-template tokens that M-rerank reads with each candidate.

pool_gpu.note: The retrieval pool (M-embed, M-rerank) runs on H-teach-class GPUs, separate from the K3 fleet.

query_embedding_cache_ttl_s.note: TTL of query embeddings in the Redis-compatible cache (RA-19); chunk embeddings live until the chunk or the model version changes.

rerank_parallel_gpus.note: One query's rerank candidates are split across 4 M-rerank replicas in the retrieval pool, so the pairs run in parallel.

rerank_min_score.note: Of the top 20 after reranking, only chunks with M-rerank P(yes) at or above 0.5 enter the context, up to the token budget; 6 pass for the reference request.

memory_ref._about: Long-term memory of the reference user (RA-27).

record_texts.note: The two records the read path returns for the reference request (hypothetical.reference_request.memory_records_retrieved).

records_stored.note: Records the reference user has in total; only 2 pass the relevance threshold for this request.

read_top_k.note: Most records the read path returns per turn.

read_min_cosine.note: Records below this similarity to the query are not injected.

token_cap.note: Hard cap on the memory message in the context.

dedupe_cosine.note: A new candidate record above this similarity to an existing record updates that record instead of adding one.

context_budget_ref._about: Context-construction budget of the reference system (Part 5.6, 5.7).

history_turn_tokens.note: Turns 1-3 of the conversation (user message plus final assistant answer, no reasoning); sum equals hypothetical.reference_request.history_tokens.

rag_chunk_tokens.note: The 6 chunks that survive rerank and trim for the reference request, each inside RA-22's 300-800 range.

rag_token_budget.note: Most tokens the orchestrator gives to retrieved chunks in one turn; chunks are added in rerank order until the next one would not fit.

prompt_budget_tokens.note: Orchestrator cap on prompt tokens per pass, far below K3's 1,048,576-token window, to bound prefill time, KV memory and cost.

compaction_trigger_tokens.note: History above this size triggers compaction of the oldest turns.

compaction_keep_recent_turns.note: The newest turns stay verbatim after compaction.

compaction_summary_tokens.note: Target length of the summary that replaces the older turns.

safety_metadata_tokens.note: Safety metadata (classifier labels, tenant policy flags) travels as request fields to the gateway and orchestrator, not as context tokens.
